newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia defends national car policy.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia defends national car policy.

text.p: Indonesia's Trade and Industry Minister Tunky Ariwibowo said on Tuesday all sides in a dispute over Jakarta's national car policy were considering what further steps to take to resolve the issue.

Japan, the United States and the European Union have challenged the policy at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) saying tax and tariff breaks to the Indonesian and South Korean companies involved contravene free trade regulations.
Ariwibowo said he had met representatives of the three complainants on the sidelines of the recent ministerial meeting of the WTO in Singapore.
"I tried to explain again about the background of our policy and how we implemented the policy and what were our objectives," he said.

"I asked them to consider our reasons and each party involved, including us, are thinking about what further steps to take to solve this problem," he told reporters after giving a briefing on the WTO meeting.

The government gave tax and tariff breaks to a company controlled by President Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra this year to produce a national car in a venture with South Korea's Kia Motors Corp.
"Our policy is unchanged. We are confident that the objective of our policy is correct. We are protected by articles in the WTO itself," the minister added.

During the briefing on the WTO ministerial meeting, Ariwibowo defended Indonesia's support for an information technology agreement aimed at eliminating tariffs on computer and telecommunications technology.
He said he believed Indonesia's "attractive" economic policies would attract global producers to Indonesia.
"The global information technology industry already knows about our policies and know that we offer efficient policy-making along with a large market," he said.
